review.method: Acceptance suite run locally with the retail capability; this harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, and a second production run of cs_app::stunts::survey_retail_stunt_authority over every reader archive of the installation (authority-census.json). Claim is implemented only: the earning-authority surface is measured, but WHICH AIRCRAFT the original credits for a zone crossing is not recorded by any file, so RetailStuntAuthoritySurvey::earning_authority_is_measured() is false and no original rule is claimed. LIMITS OF WHAT WAS MEASURED, each outside this task's scope and recorded in docs/findings/2026-10-02-t465-ai-stunt-earning.md: (1) no original executable was run, so nothing here is evidence of the original's runtime behaviour — whether a player crossing fires a stunt, whether TRAVELERS' first field is a subject and whether an AI crossing can earn one are all unknown; (2) the zone-crossing predicate, the direction and clearance rules (task #464 and the F42 rule work), the payout, the repeat policy and the linked photo are unmeasured; (3) TRAVELERS' integer subject is a bare index that is NOT decoded; (4) aiv.zrd and egen.zrd were read while searching for an authority and deliberately not decoded, because their record layouts have ~90 opaque fields each; (5) the campaign dzones.zrd semantics (objective_numbers, disable, nosnapshot) remain unmeasured — task #513 owns that member's framing. `unknowns` is empty because the measurement itself has nothing unresolved: every objective key, machine key, stunt condition, traveller condition and scenario declaration the survey reports was read to its end. Validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass.
